name: libmodbus
why: A portable Modbus library, a door into industrial control protocols that most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: libmodbus is a free C library for talking to devices that speak the Modbus protocol, over either a serial port (RTU) or an Ethernet connection (TCP). It is a library, not an application: a program links against it and calls its functions to send and receive Modbus data. The README says it runs on Linux, Mac OS X, FreeBSD, Embox, QNX and Windows, and has no dependencies.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a portable, free software way to communicate with Modbus devices. Its functions are derived from the Modicon Modbus Protocol Reference Guide. The homepage calls it "the most popular Open Source library to communicate with Modbus devices."

brief.install_notes: You need automake, autoconf, libtool and a C compiler (gcc or clang). asciidoc and xmlto are optional, for generating the documentation. The library provides a libmodbus.pc file for pkg-config. You may need to check that the install path is in /etc/ld.so.conf.d and refresh the library cache with ldconfig. Windows: MinGW and MSYS, or the Visual C project in ./src/win32/ (see ./src/win32/README.md). Embox RTOS builds use Embox's own build system. The README mentions a Homebrew command on macOS but no formula name, so the brew install line was not confirmed for this formula.
brief.standout: It covers both serial (RTU) and Ethernet (TCP) Modbus in one dependency-free C library, and it is presented as having security audits and strong test coverage. It also runs on MCUs under the Embox RTOS, which is unusual for a library with a desktop-style build.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is limited. The README has a live-looking GitHub Actions build badge and a Coverity Scan badge, and the homepage is current. I found no release date or last-commit date in either page, so I cannot confirm a recent release.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the project's funding depends on GitHub Sponsors and on sales of a commercial "promodbus" license (750€ plus VAT for companies). The purpose of that edition is to let companies ship products without the LGPL's constraints. The library itself is LGPL v2.1 or later. The GitHub README has a placeholder-looking top heading ("A groovy modbus library"). The build needs autotools, which may be painful on Windows. The homepage says it is available for Linux (packaged), FreeBSD, Mac OS and Windows.
quotes: The most popular Open Source library to communicate with Modbus devices.
libmodbus is a free software library to send/receive data with a device which respects the Modbus protocol. This library can use a serial port or an Ethernet connection.
You can use the library on MCUs with Embox RTOS.
